title: Fictional example · A shared reading list

sections.problem: In this fictional scenario, a small reading club shares book suggestions across separate messages. Members cannot tell which suggestions the group has already considered.
sections.users: Members of a fictional reading club who want one place to suggest and choose their next book.
sections.outcomes: Members can find current suggestions and see which book the group has chosen without searching old messages. This is a proposed outcome, not a measured result.
sections.useCases:
UC-01: A member suggests a book.
UC-02: Members browse the current list.
UC-03: A member records the group’s choice.
sections.scope: A single shared list for one fictional club. Members can add a title, browse suggestions, and mark a book as chosen.
sections.nonGoals: Book purchasing, public profiles, recommendations, messaging, and multiple clubs are out of scope.
sections.inputsOutputs: Input: a book title and optional author. Output: a visible suggestion in the shared list. Empty titles show a clear validation message.

requirements.outcome: A suggestion is available to the whole club.
requirements.behavior: A member can add a book title to the shared list.
requirements.acceptance: Given a nonempty title, when the member submits it, the new suggestion appears once in the list. An empty title is rejected with a visible message.

requirements.outcome: Members can find suggestions by title.
requirements.behavior: A member can search the list by book title.
requirements.acceptance: When a member enters a title fragment, only matching suggestions appear. An empty search shows the full list.

sections.quality: All core actions must work with a keyboard and have visible labels. Performance targets and persistence behavior are not yet decided.
sections.metrics: Proposed measure: whether members can find the chosen book without searching messages. Baseline, target, and test method are not documented.
sections.risks: The fictional club may not use the list consistently. The update workflow needs a usability check.
sections.decisions: Decide who may mark a book as chosen. Confirm the proposed priorities. Define how shared changes persist.
sections.evidence: This entire example is invented for demonstration. No interviews, usage measurements, real organizations, or personal information are included.
